prs.author: chirag1603
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #7394

On `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/cluster`, when `Validate` and `Deploy` are run as **two separate module invocations** (the recommended Azure Local pattern — validate as a gate, then deploy), the portal cluster **Deployments** blade shows **"Validate input = Unknown"** even though **Deploy** is green and the cluster is healthy.

### Root cause

The inline cluster deployment script (`src/deploy.sh`) deleted the singleton `deploymentSettings/default` resource whenever a Deploy run found it left in **Validate** mode:

```
if [ "$DEPLOYMENT_MODE" = "Validate" ]; then
    echo "Removing stale Validate-mode resource..."
    az resource delete --ids ".../deploymentSettings/default"
```

Deleting and recreating the resource in Deploy-only mode discards the RP-reported `reportedProperties.validationStatus` written during Validate, so the portal "Validate input" tile has nothing to read → **Unknown**.

### Why the delete is avoidable (grounded)

The `Validate` → `Deploy` transition updates the **same** resource in place — no delete is required:

- **Azure Quickstart** [`create-cluster`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-quickstart-templates/tree/master/quickstarts/microsoft.azurestackhci/create-cluster) exposes a single `deploymentMode` parameter (`Validate` | `Deploy`, default `Validate`, *"First must pass Validate prior running Deploy"*) and **redeploys the same resource** with the mode changed — no delete step.
- **[ARM deployment modes (Microsoft Learn)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/deployment-modes):** the default Incremental mode **updates resources in place and deletes nothing** unless type/location changes or Complete mode is used.
- **This module's own nested loop** (`modules/deployment-setting.bicep`) already transitions `Validate` → `Deploy` on the same `default` singleton via two sequential deployments (`@batchSize(1)`, Validate first) with **no delete** — proving the in-place transition works.

### The change

In `src/deploy.sh`, a **succeeded** Validate resource is no longer deleted — the script redeploys `Deploy` over it in place, preserving `validationStatus`. A **non-succeeded/stale** Validate resource is still removed (clean-retry safeguard). `main.json` was regenerated via `Set-AVMModule`.

This is **cosmetic and preventive**: it does not repair already-deployed clusters (a `Deploy + Succeeded` singleton hits the script's idempotency skip), but it keeps both portal tiles green for future deployments.

### Testing

- `Set-AVMModule` regenerated `main.json` (script is inlined via `loadTextContent`); interface/README unchanged.
- `bicep lint main.bicep` — clean (exit 0); `bash -n src/deploy.sh` — clean.
- Static-validation Pester suite (`module.tests.ps1`) scoped to the module: **91 passed, 9 skipped (N/A features)**. The single failure is the pre-existing, repo-wide *"issue template alphabetical position"* check (lists only unrelated `avm/ptn/*` modules; not touched by this PR).
- No live end-to-end run: the target behavior is grounded in the sources above; an already-deployed cluster cannot exercise the changed path due to the idempotency skip.

comments_list.author: chirag1603
comments_list.body:
### Validation evidence (exercised against a live Azure Local deployment)

The rewritten `src/deploy.sh` was run end-to-end against a real Azure Local (Azure Stack HCI) cluster resource to confirm the fix behaves as intended.

**1. Two-phase split is real.**
With `deploymentOperations` including `Validate`, the script issued the validation as its **own** `az deployment group create` (a dedicated `hci-deployment-validate-<epoch>` deployment), separate from the Deploy operation — matching the ARM quickstart's "Validate first, then Deploy" flow instead of fusing both into a single deployment.

**2. `validationStatus` is retained on the resource (the actual fix).**
After the Validate phase, querying the cluster's `deploymentSettings/default` returned a **non-empty** `reportedProperties.validationStatus`:

```
deploymentMode:  Validate
validationEmpty: false      # validationStatus is populated, not wiped
```

A populated `validationStatus` is exactly what keeps the portal **"Validate input"** tile from falling back to **Unknown**. Under the previous script, a Validate-mode resource was unconditionally deleted before Deploy, which erased this record and produced the Unknown tile.

**3. No delete of a succeeded Validate.**
The Deploy phase now deploys **in place** over the existing `default` resource; only a stale / non-succeeded Validate is removed. This preserves the validation record across the Validate → Deploy transition.

**Coverage.** All three `deploymentOperations` combinations — `['Validate']`, `['Deploy']`, and `['Validate','Deploy']` — follow the same in-place, no-wipe path, so both portal tiles stay populated. The module's public interface is unchanged (backward compatible), and existing idempotency semantics (`Deploy` + `Succeeded` ⇒ skip; `Deploy` + not-succeeded ⇒ fail) are preserved.

prs.author: a3burak
prs.body:
## Description

- Added the optional parameter `customerManagedKeyDbfsRoot` (`customerManagedKeyType`), which encrypts the workspace's DBFS root storage account with a customer-managed key through `properties.parameters.encryption`. Key Vault and Managed HSM keys are both supported, following the same pattern as `customerManagedKey` and `customerManagedKeyManagedDisk`.
- Added the output `storageAccountIdentityPrincipalId`, the identity of the DBFS root storage account that needs access to that key. It is available once `prepareEncryption` is enabled, matching how `managedDiskIdentityPrincipalId` is exposed for the managed disk key.
- Added the e2e test `cmk-dbfs`.

### Why

The module supports customer-managed keys for managed services and managed disks, but not for the third feature Azure Databricks offers, the DBFS root. A workspace that must use customer-managed keys for all data at rest, as PCI DSS and similar regimes expect, cannot be expressed through the module today.

The storage account identity is created by the provider when `prepareEncryption` is set, and it must hold `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` on the key before the key is applied. The module had that identity commented out as read only and did not output it, so a caller had no way to grant it without reading the resource back separately.

### How it is used

The key cannot be applied in the same deployment that first creates the identity, because the grant has to exist in between. The new test shows the sequence:

1. Deploy the workspace with `prepareEncryption: true`.
2. Grant `storageAccountIdentityPrincipalId` `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` on the key.
3. Deploy the workspace again with `customerManagedKeyDbfsRoot` (then an idempotency run).

Without `keyVersion` the storage account follows the latest key version. Verified outside this repository on a VNet-injected premium workspace: all three customer-managed key features enabled together, a redeploy that omits `parameters.encryption` leaves the DBFS root key in place (no write reaches the storage account), and jobs run normally afterwards.

### Compatibility

Additive. The parameter is optional and the encryption block is written through a conditional spread, so callers that do not set it produce the same request body as before. `parameters.encryption` exists at the module's current API version `2024-05-01`; the module builds free of BCP diagnostics.

### Relation to #7381

Independent of #7381 (API version `2026-01-01` and `computeMode`), and based on `main`. Both bump `version.json` to `0.13` and touch `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` and `main.json`, so whichever merges second needs a rebase and the next minor version. Happy to rebase this one onto #7381 instead if the reviewer prefers a single release.

## Description

Addresses the pre-deployment regional recovery gap exposed by the [BAMI Lab canary run](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36429053903). This is a standalone change from `main`, not stacked on [#7405](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7405). That review, its branch and its trigger label are unchanged.

### Behavior

- Query resource-provider metadata with an explicit namespace. [The cmdlet documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/az.resources/get-azresourceprovider) confirms that unqualified enumeration returns registered providers only. Missing metadata is no longer treated as global or sent to excluded WestEurope. The approved region list is unchanged.
- Before deployment, allow at most **three total validation attempts in distinct supported, allowed, nonexcluded regions**. Retry only wholly regional errors: `RequestDisallowedByAzure` with the `locationineligible` link, or narrowly classified regional capacity/availability errors. Mixed, malformed, unknown, permission, authentication, configuration and assertion errors stop.
- Restore pristine region-token inputs after each failed attempt. The successful candidate is used consistently in template parameters, referenced token files, the validation output and the subsequent deployment.
- Keep explicit custom, CI-parameter and token locations pinned; conflicting pins fail. Explicitly global resources retain their resource-group/metadata location. Resource-group-scope validation does not relocate or recreate a group to enable recovery.
- Keep deployment retries **outside** the regional-validation loop: deployment starts only after successful validation, and its existing maximum of three attempts stays in that validated region. There is no post-deployment regional failover, resource-deletion redesign, assertion retry, or change to retention/deployment-name cleanup. Cancellation stops further attempts.
- Document the contract in the composite-action descriptions and the directly related PowerShell help. Preserve subscription selection, authentication and secure CI-parameter handling.

The specific reason provider enumeration was empty in the historical canary is not asserted as proven. Offline fixtures reproduce the missing-registered-provider case and the observed regional validation error; no live provider lookup or canary rerun was performed.

## Pipeline Reference

| Pipeline |
| -------- |
| Local offline validation of `3feab0ae188000ffb1d11ace9d6ac5bd7eb68332`: **135 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** |
| PowerShell parsing and `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Severity Error`: **8 files, zero errors** |
| `npm exec --offline --no -- prettier --check '.github\actions\templates\avm-validateModuleDeployment\action.yml'`: passed |
| `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check`: passed |

Before/after evidence: the same selector regression fails against the original code because it returns `WestEurope` instead of an eligible region, and passes against this change. Runtime integration tests execute the actual action scripts and helpers with mocked Azure/network operations, including candidate/token propagation, bounded exhaustion, cancellation, cleanup failures and unchanged same-region deployment retry ownership.

Reproduce the focused suite from the repository root:

```powershell
Import-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.0
Import-Module powershell-yaml
$configuration = New-PesterConfiguration
$configuration.Run.Path = @(
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\Get-AvailableResourceLocation.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\RegionalValidationWorkflow.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\CIParameterWorkflow.Tests.ps1'
    '.\utilities\tests\pipelines\TestSubscriptionWorkflow.Tests.ps1'
)
$configuration.Run.PassThru = $true
$configuration.Output.Verbosity = 'Normal'
$result = Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration
if ($result.FailedCount -gt 0 -or $result.FailedContainersCount -gt 0) {
    throw 'Regional retry regressions failed.'
}
```

**No Azure deployment or live setting change was performed. Do not add `PR: Run Checks` as part of this source-only review.** Live validation requires a separate decision; the failed canary has not been rerun.

## Summary

Source-only fixes for the Lab fixture incident documented in [#7405](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7405) and [run 36482752869](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36482752869). The initial `StorageAccountAlreadyTaken` failure is distinct from the later cleanup delay and credential-expiry symptoms. This change does not modify or claim to validate regional recovery.

- Give the max fixture's storage dependency a 16-character name derived from `uniqueString(resourceGroup.id, serviceShort)`. The subscription/resource-group/fixture scope determines the name, not the changing deployment-attempt name. Initial, repeat and retry deployments keep the same name. No public module API, version, resources, assertions or generated README changes.
- Retain every attempted `DeploymentNames` entry. Add optional `PreflightRejectedDeploymentNames` metadata only for a narrowly recognized, top-level Azure preflight rejection naming that exact submission. Nested `DeploymentFailed` errors, unknown/null submission results, context failures and cancellation are not evidence of preflight rejection.
- Pass that metadata through the existing composite action to cleanup. A marked attempt skips lookup retries only when the exact deployment query returns HTTP 404 with `DeploymentNotFound`. If a record exists, including a failed/partial deployment, it is still inspected and cleaned. Callers without metadata retain strict lookup behavior.
- Keep bounded discovery for required missing records: at most 40 discovery rounds, with the existing 60-second interval between rounds. Unclassified 404s, authentication, permission, transport and malformed-response failures remain explicit rather than becoming safe absence. Clean already discovered resources before reporting unresolved lookup failures, including failures in a later nested lookup. Zero discovered resources does not hide unresolved required names; a genuinely empty resolved deployment remains valid.

## Description

Add an isolated, **manual-only** Bicep README drift preview. The new helper compares the 574 source-backed READMEs using `Invoke-AvmDocs -CheckDrift -IncludeRenderedContent`, preserves three source-less READMEs by exact path, byte length, and SHA-256, and permits only the eight pinned historical Key Vault comment lines. All other drift, rendering errors, missing paths, or coverage mismatches fail closed.

For changed `main.bicep`/`main.json`, compile all source-backed Bicep sources in the affected top-level module, including nested `/modules` children, using the tool-managed checksum-pinned Bicep CLI in the disposable checkout. Validate against the freshly compiled JSON and fail if checked-in `main.json` was stale. README-only and template/config-only checks use the existing committed compiled JSON, avoiding historical compiler-version churn. Root `bicepconfig.json` and tracked `docs/templates/avm-readme-v1.scriban` each select the full 574-source-backed set.

The workflow has **only `workflow_dispatch`** and `contents: read`: no automatic pull-request or push trigger, Azure authentication, OIDC, deployment, publishing, or release tags. The existing `Set-AVMModule`, module Pester/composite validation, deployment matrix, preview workflow, and README push exclusions are unchanged. This workflow was not dispatched.

A disposable checkout of this exact head `c87647608c85d1477945eeb9d73ff69106132e90` contains all 55 files byte-matched to the published asset head `36e9641e5ee04bde8a38faf234b848b49eea4530`: root `bicepconfig.json`, `docs/templates/avm-readme-v1.scriban` (SHA-256 `3099E02E1DB7B637F0ABA462E2213C9225DC9769C7000E8CF741F440695DAF34`), and 53 Notes. The imported authoring source checkout HEAD is the approved `4962cd619347e2c111e50a3db0ae591081092ecd`, manifest SHA-256 `2B6ECA01F8852829EB5351591A0C384309CB6DCA2C56E05D901430D24B56EE66`; the tool-managed Bicep CLI reports `0.47.16`.

prs.body:
## Description

Updates the Azure Stack HCI resources in `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/cluster` from `2026-04-30` to the GA API version `2026-10-01`.

| Resource type | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/clusters` | `2026-04-30` | `2026-10-01` |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/clusters/deploymentSettings` | `2026-04-30` | `2026-10-01` |
| `Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/edgeDevices` | `2026-04-30` | `2026-10-01` |

This covers every place these versions are used: the resource declarations, the `existing` cluster in the `deployment-setting` child module, the `reference(.../edgeDevices/default, ...)` call that resolves `physicalNodes[].ipv4Address`, and the resource-derived type of the `tags` parameter. No other API versions change.

`version.json` is already `0.6` (from #7384) and `0.6.0` has not been published yet (latest is `0.5.0`), so the change is folded into the existing `0.6.0` entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Schema impact: no parameter changes

A diff of the PUT body schemas of the three resource types between the [`2026-04-30`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/9bf19532443271e5c02c7968bea48ba632b749ad/specification/azurestackhci/resource-manager/Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/StackHCI/stable/2026-04-30/hci.json) and [`2026-10-01`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/9bf19532443271e5c02c7968bea48ba632b749ad/specification/azurestackhci/resource-manager/Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/StackHCI/stable/2026-10-01/hci.json) specifications (added in Azure/azure-rest-api-specs#44812), resolving `$ref`, `allOf` and the `kind` discriminator, shows:

| Resource type | Writable changes | Read-only additions | Removed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clusters` | None | `sdnProperties` | None |
| `clusters/deploymentSettings` | `eceSecretName` gains `chapCredential` and `mutualChapCredential` | `percentComplete`, `error`, `additionalData`, `recommendedSteps` on validation and deployment steps | None |
| `edgeDevices` | None | `reportedProperties.networkProfile.sdnProperties` | None |

- The two new `eceSecretName` values are documented as "iSCSI CHAP authentication during edge machine node preparation". They belong to the new `edgeMachines` resource types in `2026-10-01`, not to the Arc machine and edge device flow this module uses, and the enum is extensible (`modelAsString: true`).
- All 70 property paths the module sets or reads exist unchanged in `2026-10-01`. The values the module restricts with `@allowed` (`deploymentMode`, `operationType`, storage `configurationMode`) are unchanged.
- No parameters or outputs are added, renamed, or removed.

### Why move to `2026-10-01` now

#7384 kept these resources on `2026-04-30` because Bicep has no type definitions for `2026-10-01`, which disables compile-time property validation for them. That is still the case in Bicep `0.47.16`. This PR adopts the GA version anyway, and closes that gap with the schema diff above and an end-to-end deployment on a live cluster (below).

Until a Bicep release includes the `2026-10-01` types, the build reports 5 non-blocking warnings (`main` currently has none). They go away without code changes once the types ship:

- `BCP081` (×4): no types available for `clusters`, `edgeDevices` and `clusters/deploymentSettings` at `2026-10-01`.
- `BCP321` (×1): `tags: tags` on the cluster resource, a side effect of the missing types.

The AVM API-version test will also warn, because AVM's `apiSpecsList.json` does not list `2026-10-01` yet. That test is warning-only.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule` regenerated `main.json` and the READMEs; running it again produces no changes.
- Static validation (`module.tests.ps1`) for this module: 92 passed, 0 failed.
- Validated end-to-end with a successful Validate and Deploy run on an Azure Local cluster.

### Related

- #7395 also changes this module's `CHANGELOG.md` and `main.json`. Whichever merges second needs a rebase and a fresh `Set-AVMModule` run.

## Description

# Static Site Private DNS Deployment Issue

## Initial Issue

The deployment failed with the following errors:

`Warning BCP318:
The value of type "module | null" may be null at the start of the deployment.`
`Error InvalidTemplate:
The template resource '...-staticSite-PrivateEndpoint-0' reference to
'...-staticSite-PrivateDnsZone' requires an API version.`

The affected code in modules/Microsoft.Web/static-site/main.bicep was:
`privateDnsZoneGroup: privateEndpoint.?privateDnsZoneGroup ?? {
  privateDnsZoneGroupConfigs: [
    {
      privateDnsZoneResourceId: staticSite_privateDnsZone.outputs.resourceId
    }
  ]
}`

### Root Cause
The staticSite_privateDnsZone module is deployed conditionally:
`createPrivateDnsZone == 'Enabled'`

When createPrivateDnsZone is set to Disabled, the module is not deployed. However, the fallback expression in the ?? operator still contains a reference to the module:
`staticSite_privateDnsZone.outputs.resourceId`

The Bicep ?? operator is compiled to the ARM coalesce() function. ARM can evaluate the fallback expression even when an existing privateDnsZoneGroup has already been supplied.

As a result, ARM attempts to resolve a reference to a module that was not deployed. Since the reference does not contain a resolvable API version, the deployment fails with the InvalidTemplate error.

The same reference also causes warning BCP318, because the conditional module can be null.

### Solution
The module reference must be placed inside a conditional expression:
`privateDnsZoneGroup: privateEndpoint.?privateDnsZoneGroup ?? (createPrivateDnsZone == 'Enabled'
  ? {
      privateDnsZoneGroupConfigs: [
        {
          privateDnsZoneResourceId: staticSite_privateDnsZone!.outputs.resourceId
        }
      ]
    }
  : null)`

The expression now behaves as follows:

If privateEndpoint.privateDnsZoneGroup is provided, that configuration is used.
If no DNS zone group is provided and createPrivateDnsZone is Enabled, the resource ID of the newly created DNS zone is used.
If no DNS zone group is provided and createPrivateDnsZone is Disabled, the value is set to null.

## Description

Source-only fix for request timeouts bypassing deployment cleanup. The original [workflow run](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36690626584/attempts/1) and [IP Group defaults job](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36690626584/job/109807448282) remain failed: the deployment command timed out and normal cleanup was skipped. An independently completed ARM deployment is not treated as a successful CI run.

The submission and discovery paths previously treated every `OperationCanceledException`, including `TaskCanceledException` with a typed `TimeoutException`, as cancellation. Submission could therefore escape before the composite action wrote its cleanup outputs; discovery could discard already identified resources.

- Distinguish typed request/deadline timeouts from genuine cancellation through inner exceptions, PowerShell error-record wrappers, and aggregate errors. Unclassified cancellation and `PipelineStoppedException` still stop further work; timeout wording alone does not override cancellation.
- Keep timeouts and unknown, missing, or nonterminal submission results explicitly failed, without another deployment submission. Preserve every actually attempted name and prior preflight-rejection metadata. Failures before submission do not create fictitious cleanup names. Confirmed failed results, the exact Az `DeploymentFailed` message for the attempted deployment, and confirmed preflight rejections retain the existing maximum of three same-region attempts.
- Emit deployment-name arrays before the action reports failure, leaving the output empty when nothing was submitted. Keep the existing cleanup, cancellation, and resource-retention condition unchanged.
- Retain known cleanup targets when discovery times out and report the lookup failure after scoped removal. A timeout cannot be accepted as `DeploymentNotFound`, even if an error record carries that ID. Empty exception messages no longer initiate an unguarded diagnostic lookup that could lose ownership metadata.

**Offline validation:** 326 tests passed, zero failed or skipped, on commit `abb8fd8c9771ac4312185d0b5c4341dfc41c8098` (base `695f0a85419c8521206b461e914bf5c54fcfddf8`), using PowerShell 7.6.6 and Pester 5.7.1. The existing baseline passed 64 cleanup/regional tests; the first added regression set reproduced 26 failures before the source fix.

The passing suites are `DeploymentCleanupWorkflow`, `RegionalValidationWorkflow`, `Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry`, `Get-AvailableResourceLocation`, `CIParameterWorkflow`, `Get-CIParameterMap`, `Get-TestSubscriptionList`, `TestSubscriptionWorkflow`, and `Get-OrderedResourcesList`. Coverage executes the actual composite-action scripts and cleanup condition with mocked Azure boundaries, including typed timeout wrappers after acceptance, earlier partial attempts, all four scopes, strict absence handling, discovery failures, secure-input redaction, retention, and a real stopped PowerShell runspace. Changed PowerShell ranges pass formatting; parsing and PSScriptAnalyzer introduce no errors or new warnings.

**Scope and limits:** No live Azure/Entra calls or jobs, auth refresh, timeout increases, execution labels, module fixtures, APIs, versions, tenant selectors, permissions, or publication behavior were changed. No recovery-to-success or background retry mechanism was added. The original log does not establish its exception-type chain; the offline regressions exercise the relevant typed .NET shapes. Live qualification remains intentionally unperformed, and this source is held as a draft.

## Pipeline Reference

| Pipeline |
| -------- |
| [Original failing workflow, attempt 1](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36690626584/attempts/1) — historical evidence only; not rerun or counted as green. |

No new live pipeline was requested. Validation for this source change was offline only.

  - [ ] Feature update backwards compatible feature updates, and I have bumped the MINOR version in `version.json`.
  - [ ] Breaking changes and I have bumped the MAJOR version in `version.json`.
  - [ ] Update to documentation
- [x] Update to CI Environment or utilities (Non-module affecting changes)

## Checklist

- [ ] I have run `Set-AVMModule` locally to generate the supporting module files. Not applicable: no module changes.
- [ ] My corresponding pipelines / checks run clean and green without any errors or warnings. Live validation intentionally not run; offline results are recorded above.

## Description

Updates `avm/res/hybrid-compute/machine` and its published `extension` child module to the newest stable HybridCompute API version, `2026-07-15`.

| Module | Resource type | From | To | Version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hybrid-compute/machine` | `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines` | `2025-01-13` | `2026-07-15` | `0.6.0` |
| `hybrid-compute/machine/extension` | `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines/extensions` (and the referenced parent `machines`) | `2025-01-13` | `2026-07-15` | `0.2.0` |

The other resource types in the module are already on their newest stable API versions (`Microsoft.GuestConfiguration/guestConfigurationAssignments` `2024-04-05`, `Microsoft.Authorization/locks` `2020-05-01`, `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments` `2022-04-01`).

### Schema impact: no parameter changes

A diff of the PUT body schemas between the [`2025-01-13`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/85efeb3571600039a5ab10b03ea217f637c4720e/specification/hybridcompute/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridCompute/HybridCompute/stable/2025-01-13/HybridCompute.json) and [`2026-07-15`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/85efeb3571600039a5ab10b03ea217f637c4720e/specification/hybridcompute/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridCompute/HybridCompute/stable/2026-07-15/openapi.json) specifications shows:

| Resource type | Writable additions | Read-only additions | Removed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machines` | `identity.userAssignedIdentities`, `properties.hardwareResourceId` | `properties.statusReason`, `clientId` / `principalId` of user-assigned identities | None |
| `machines/extensions` | None | None | None |

- Every property path the two modules set or read exists unchanged in `2026-07-15`, so no parameters or outputs are added, renamed, or removed. The new optional properties are not exposed by this change.
- `identity.type` gains `UserAssigned` values; the module keeps using `SystemAssigned`.
- `vmId` is now documented as a `uuid`, and `parentClusterResourceId` and `privateLinkScopeResourceId` as ARM IDs. The module's empty-string defaults for these are still accepted: the service generates the `vmId`.

### Versioning

Both modules get a MINOR bump, as the module's previous API version update (`2024-07-10` → `2025-01-13`) did with `0.5.0`: `machine` `0.5` → `0.6` and `extension` `0.1` → `0.2`, with matching `CHANGELOG.md` entries.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule -Recurse` regenerated `main.json` and the READMEs; running it again produces no changes.
- Static validation (`module.tests.ps1`) for the module and its `extension` child: 155 passed, 0 failed. Bicep types are available for `2026-07-15` (no compile warnings), and AVM's API version list includes it.
- Validated end-to-end with a successful deployment of an `HCI` Arc machine using the module defaults in an Azure Local environment, and a re-deployment that changed nothing. The `extension` child module is validated statically; deploying it requires an Arc machine with a connected agent.

### Related

`avm/res/azure-stack-hci/virtual-machine-instance` consumes this module (currently `0.4.1`); it will be updated in a separate PR once `0.6.0` is published.

## Description

Fixes the failed publishing of `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/virtual-machine-instance` `0.2.0` after #7429.

The module pipeline on `main` ([run 36736704112](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36736704112)) failed the static test *"Set-ModuleReadMe script should not apply any updates"*, so `0.2.0` was not published. The README's "Cross-referenced modules" section still listed `br/public:avm/res/hybrid-compute/machine:0.4.1`, while `main.bicep` references `0.6.0` since #7429. The README had been generated with a stale local cross-reference cache: the README tooling caches cross-references in a temporary file for up to a day.

This PR regenerates the README with a fresh cache. The only change is that line, `0.4.1` → `0.6.0`. There are no module code changes: `version.json` stays `0.2`, and `0.2.0` remains the unpublished target version with its existing `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule` with fresh caches produces no further changes.
- The module workflow ran on this branch with static validation only ([run 36740648686](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36740648686)): all static tests, including *"Set-ModuleReadMe script should not apply any updates"*, and all PSRule checks passed.

### After merge

The module workflow's `push` trigger ignores `README.md` changes, so merging this PR does not start the pipeline. To publish `0.2.0`, the `avm.res.azure-stack-hci.virtual-machine-instance` workflow needs to be run manually on `main` after the merge.

- No writable properties are added or removed.
- The read-only `inboundConnectivityState` is removed.
- `kind` no longer accepts `AWS` and `GCP`. The module always deploys `kind: 'ProvisionedCluster'`, which is unchanged.

Every property the module sets exists unchanged in `2026-05-01`, so no parameters or outputs are added, renamed, or removed. The one exception, `gateway.resourceId`, isn't a change: it is also absent from `2026-02-01-preview` (the API dropped it in `2025-08-01-preview`), and Bicep already reports `BCP037` for it on `main`.

The cluster provisioned successfully and reached `Connected`; Entra ID with Azure RBAC, OIDC issuer and workload identity were enabled. A re-deployment to the running cluster also succeeded without changing its settings.

## Description

Fix a cross-resource-group naming collision risk in the shared diagnostic test dependency helper. Storage account names now combine up to 11 base-name characters with a 13-character `uniqueString(resourceGroup().id, fullBase)` suffix (maximum 24 characters). Event Hubs namespace names combine up to 36 base-name characters, a hyphen, and the same form of suffix (maximum 50 characters).

The suffix is a deterministic, pseudorandom-looking hash, not cryptographic randomness or a guarantee against collisions. Names remain stable for the same resource group and inputs across initial deployments, repeat deployments, and retries. Including the full base name in the hash differentiates inputs that share a truncated prefix. Parameter descriptions explain this behavior.

Only the shared test helper and its regression tests change. Resource-group-scoped names, resources, role conditions, output IDs, and API versions are unchanged. No public AVM module, README, version, or generated module JSON changes.

- Tests compile the actual helper and naming expressions, covering scope isolation, repeat/retry stability, full-base hashing, truncation, valid characters, length boundaries, and unchanged scoped names/output IDs.

prs.author: jaredfholgate
prs.body:
## Description

Use one generic validation-settings interface in all three reusable module workflows. Remove the tenant selector based on repository identity or module canaries: the consumer no longer reads `AVM_TEST_TENANT`, `TEST_BAMI_MODULE_PATHS`, or `TEST_BAMI_*` execution settings. Existing repository checks that protect release/tag creation are unchanged.

Execution identifiers may be configured as GitHub **Variables or Secrets**, with Variables taking precedence. The coordinated Tools publisher will use the canonical, nonsecret `VALIDATE_*` **Variables**. Actual credential JSON, passwords, and private keys are not moved to Variables; `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` remains Secrets-only.

### Identifier resolution and compatibility

| Setting | Resolution order |
| --- | --- |
| Client | `vars.VALIDATE_CLIENT_ID`, then `secrets.VALIDATE_CLIENT_ID` |
| Tenant | `vars.VALIDATE_TENANT_ID`, then `secrets.VALIDATE_TENANT_ID` |
| Subscription pool | `vars.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS`, `vars.TEST_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS`, `secrets.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS`, `secrets.TEST_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS` |
| Optional singleton | `vars.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, then `secrets.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`; used only when no pool is configured |
| Management group | `vars.VALIDATE_MANAGEMENT_GROUP_ID`, `vars.ARM_MGMTGROUP_ID`, `secrets.VALIDATE_MANAGEMENT_GROUP_ID`, `secrets.ARM_MGMTGROUP_ID` |
| Persistent subscription | The publisher's canonical name is `VALIDATE_PERSISTENT_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`. These actions do not introduce a new input, required field, or token for this previously unused setting. |

Canonical names win within each namespace; Variables win across the existing aliases before Secrets. The values are mapped into the existing action inputs and runtime environment names. A supplied malformed pool is rejected, and a nonempty whitespace pool fails at the action boundary instead of silently selecting a singleton. The generic subscription helper API is unchanged.

### Authentication and contributor capabilities

Default OIDC authentication requires only its existing client and tenant identifiers, plus the selected subscription. It does not gain an unrelated management-group or five-setting requirement.

The existing service-principal exception path and both exception login steps remain available. When that path is used, credentials must be a JSON object with nonempty string `clientId`, `clientSecret`, and `tenantId` fields. Errors do not dump the credential payload. If `VALIDATE_TENANT_ID` is explicitly resolved, the credential tenant must match it case-insensitively. A **different same-tenant exception principal remains supported**; client equality is not imposed. Extra credential properties and selected-subscription replacement are preserved. Credential-only exception configurations remain supported when no separate tenant/client is configured. Exception paths and their descendants do not fall back to OIDC when credentials are missing, malformed, or inconsistent.

PSRule resolves a pool or singleton when configured and retains its optional static/no-auth behavior when neither is supplied. No new credential requirement is added to static analysis.

**Key Vault support is preserved.** The optional `KeyVaultName` API, existing `CI_KEY_VAULT_NAME` configuration and deprecation warning, vault lookup, GitHub CI_ secret-over-variable-over-vault precedence, type conversion, redaction, subscription fallback API, composite `managementGroupId` inputs, and selected-subscription reuse remain intact. Earlier out-of-scope removals were reversed and are not part of the final change.

### LIVE CUTOVER HOLD

Source publication does not authorize or perform runtime configuration changes. The coordinating parent must stage and verify the five canonical `VALIDATE_*` Variables, inspect collisions and effective inputs, and coordinate migration before resuming consumer execution. These names can be staged without overwriting the old `TEST_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS` or `ARM_MGMTGROUP_ID` settings used by unchanged maintenance workflows. Historical `TEST_BAMI_*` settings stay intact until their consumers migrate; this change does not delete them.

If canonical settings are missing, configured compatibility aliases or Secrets can become effective. The generic consumer **does not independently know which tenant is BAMI**. An `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` value used for an exception must target the explicitly declared tenant; credential-only configurations cannot be independently checked against an absent declared tenant. Operators must also review the intended `CI_KEY_VAULT_NAME` and its access in the chosen tenant. No existing secret is queried, deleted, or repaired by this source change.

## Final source scope

Against original baseline `82bab0404566557b9fb5efdc9780bb5ce438030b`, exactly six files change:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/avm.template.module.yml` | Generic Variables-first identifier bindings; no tenant selector. |
| `.github/workflows/avm.template.module.preview.yml` | The same generic bindings. |
| `.github/workflows/avm.template.module.publish.yml` | The same generic bindings. |
| `.github/actions/templates/avm-validateModuleDeployment/action.yml` | Method-required authentication checks, explicit tenant consistency, and supplied-pool whitespace rejection. |
| `.github/actions/templates/avm-validateModulePSRule/action.yml` | Optional generic pool/singleton resolution without a provider-specific branch. |
| `utilities/tests/pipelines/TestSubscriptionWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | Synthetic source/alias precedence, preserved capability, safe authentication-failure, and optional-static cases. |

Standalone PSRule/history workflows, generic helpers, other capability/regression tests, all module fixtures/APIs/versions, and the removed five-setting helper remain unchanged from the restored baseline. Nine specifically preserved files are byte/blob-identical to that baseline. No input API, normal trigger, fork/trust boundary, protected environment, permission, fixture matrix, `e2eIgnore`, release/tag guard, concurrency rule, retry policy, cancellation rule, or resource/history-cleanup behavior is removed.

## Pipeline Reference

| Offline verification | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Seven covering Pester suites | **588 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped** |
| Workflow lint | All three reusable workflows pass actionlint |
| YAML/PowerShell parsing | 5 YAML files, 1 PowerShell file, 20 embedded scripts |
| Focused formatting/analyzer/whitespace | Pass; synthetic Key Vault test values have an explicit fixture-only analyzer suppression |
| Guard/interface proof | 562 unchanged workflow/action properties checked against baseline |
| Scope/capability proof | Exactly six files; nine preserved files remain byte/blob-identical |

Suites: `TestSubscriptionWorkflow`, `Get-TestSubscriptionList`, `CIParameterWorkflow`, `Get-CIParameterMap`, `RegionalValidationWorkflow`, `DeploymentCleanupWorkflow`, and `ModuleWorkflow`.

The tests cover Variables-only, Secrets-only, both sources, cross-alias precedence, optional singleton fallback, retired-selector independence, malformed preferred values, Key Vault warning/lookup/precedence, separate same-tenant exception principals, credential-only exceptions, mismatched tenants, safe credential errors, optional static PSRule, and existing retry/cleanup/fork/release behavior. Azure/network boundaries are mocked. No Azure authentication, cloud queries, deployments, manual workflow runs, live configuration changes, or blanket module test sweep were performed. Source CI is not evidence that all modules passed live end-to-end tests.

Exact tested head: `d4749cee573741524fc478b10ff199cdc9ee3149`.

Exact tested tree: `28a60606fb08e8fad88f7248c13028c1ba0269d1`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Update to CI Environment or utilities (Non-module affecting changes)

## Checklist

- [x] Reused the same open review and branch with a normal follow-up commit; no amend, rebase, or force push.
- [x] Preserved the externally selected ready-for-review state and existing labels; no auto-merge enabled.
- [x] Verified the exact source scope and offline tests on the committed tree.
- [ ] `Set-AVMModule` / module CHANGELOG updates — not applicable; no Bicep modules changed.
- [ ] Live namespace cutover or module deployments — on hold, not performed.

The coordinating parent retains responsibility for review, merge, and every live configuration decision. This source publication performs none of those actions.

prs.body:
## Description

Updates `avm/res/hybrid-container-service/provisioned-cluster-instance` so that the unpublished `0.3.0` can create clusters on Azure Local and passes the static tests again: it updates the referenced `connected-cluster` module, the Key Vault and telemetry API versions, and keeps `provisionedClusterInstances` on the stable `2024-01-01`.

| Resource type or reference | Published `0.2.1` | `main` (unpublished `0.3.0`) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.HybridContainerService/provisionedClusterInstances` | `2024-01-01` | `2026-04-01-preview` | `2024-01-01` |
| `avm/res/kubernetes/connected-cluster` (module and its 4 imported types) | `0.1.1` | `0.1.1` | `0.3.0` (deploys `connectedClusters` at `2026-05-01`) |
| `Microsoft.Kubernetes/connectedClusters` (`existing` reference) | `2024-07-15-preview` | `2024-07-15-preview` | `2026-05-01` |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults`, `vaults/secrets` | `2023-07-01` | `2023-07-01` | `2026-02-01` |
| `Microsoft.Resources/deployments` (AVM telemetry) | `2024-03-01` | `2024-03-01` | `2025-04-01` |

### Why `provisionedClusterInstances` stays on `2024-01-01`

#6995 moved `main` to `2026-04-01-preview` and added `hciSecurityProfile` (FIPS images, custom CA trust certificates), `gpuCountPerNode` and `authorizedIPRanges`. That version was never published, because the module's pipeline has stopped at static validation since then. Creating a cluster with it fails on Azure Local:

- Azure Resource Manager accepts `2023-11-15-preview`, `2024-01-01` and `2026-04-01-preview` for this resource type.
- A create is only forwarded if the AKS Arc extension behind the Azure Local custom location supports the API version. On the Azure Local release used for validation it supports `2023-11-15-preview` to `2025-09-01-preview`, so a create at `2026-04-01-preview` fails at preflight with `MissingAzureKubernetesMapping` ("The custom location ... does not support resource type 'Microsoft.HybridContainerService/provisionedClusterInstances' with api-version '2026-04-01-preview'"). Reads at `2026-04-01-preview` work.
- The [AKS release notes for Azure Local](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks-hybrid-edge/local/aks-whats-new-local) list no AKS changes since release 2602.

`2024-01-01` is therefore the newest version that both accept, and the one the published `0.2.1` uses. It has no `securityProfile` and no `gpuCountPerNode`; the [API change log](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/templates/microsoft.hybridcontainerservice/change-log/provisionedclusterinstances) lists both as added in `2026-04-01-preview`. This PR therefore removes the `hciSecurityProfile` parameter, its exported `hciSecurityProfileType`, and `gpuCountPerNode` from `agentPoolProfileType`. None of them was ever published, so no released version breaks. `authorizedIPRanges` exists in `2024-01-01` and stays. The removed settings can come back once Azure Local supports an API version that has them.

### Schema impact

A diff of the PUT body schemas of [`2026-04-01-preview`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/b51b4e628385a62aa5199ee9bf06bb6b61a681eb/specification/hybridaks/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridContainerService/HybridContainerService/preview/2026-04-01-preview/openapi.json) and [`2024-01-01`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/b51b4e628385a62aa5199ee9bf06bb6b61a681eb/specification/hybridaks/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridContainerService/HybridContainerService/stable/2024-01-01/provisionedClusterInstances.json) shows:

- `2024-01-01` lacks `securityProfile` (and its sub-properties), `agentPoolProfiles[].gpuCountPerNode` and the read-only `status.featuresStatus`.
- `networkProfile.networkPolicy` doesn't accept `cilium` in `2024-01-01`; the module's default is `calico`, as in `0.2.1`.
- All 26 other property paths the module sets exist in `2024-01-01`.

The referenced `connected-cluster` module moves from `0.1.1` to `0.3.0`: the 4 imported types (`aadProfileType`, `arcAgentProfileType`, `oidcIssuerProfileType`, `securityProfileType`) have the same structure in both versions, and every parameter this module passes still exists. Its `0.2.0` and `0.3.0` list no breaking changes.

The Key Vault references are in `secrets.bicep` and in `nested/read.bicep` and `nested/write.bicep`, which the module's SSH-key deployment script deploys to read and store the generated key pair. #7374 updates Key Vault references in other modules to at least `2026` because of a pending API deprecation; this module wasn't included there.

### Static tests that fail on `main`

- `CHANGELOG.md` has a section for `0.2.2`, which was never published; the test only accepts published versions or the next one (`0.3.0`). Its entry ("Recompiled template") moves into `0.3.0`.
- `Set-AVMModule`, like the CI's README test, generates this module's README without the "Cross-referenced modules" section, so the committed README never matched. The README is committed as generated. The cross-reference cache records the module's `secrets.bicep` instead of `main.bicep`, which looks like a tooling issue for modules with more than one Bicep file at the root.

### Versioning

`version.json` stays `0.3`, which #6995 set and which was never published; this PR's changes are added to the `0.3.0` CHANGELOG entry. Compared with the published `0.2.1`, `0.3.0` has the same parameters, types and outputs plus the optional `authorizedIPRanges`, and keeps `provisionedClusterInstances` on `2024-01-01`.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule` regenerated `main.json` and the README; running it again with fresh caches produces no changes.

Make a small, non-behavioural source change to the SQL Managed Instance parent module so it qualifies for the normal patch-release workflow after merge. Clarify the existing `storageSizeInGB` bounds (32-32768 GB, in 32-GB increments), regenerate `main.json` and `README.md` with `Set-AVMModule`, and leave `version.json` at `0.5`. Preserve and extend the existing unreleased changelog section. CI calculates the patch version; release tagging and registry publishing still depend on successful normal validation workflows. This change does not itself publish a release.

As explicitly requested, move only the max test's `enforcedLocation` from `eastus` to `eastasia`. Keep `GP_Gen5`, `Gen5`, `GeneralPurpose`, 4 vCores and all other sizing/region settings unchanged; no ignore files are added.

Make the SQL MI instance name in all four end-to-end scenarios subscription/resource-group-aware: `${namePrefix}-${serviceShort}-${uniqueString(resourceGroup.id)}`. [SQL MI instance names have global scope](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/resource-name-rules#microsoftsql), so different test subscriptions must not deliberately reuse the same fixed instance name. The suffix uses the full resource-group ID, including the selected subscription. It stays stable for retries and the serial init/idem pair; it does not depend on deployment name, iteration, run ID or fresh randomness. Only the instance names and generated README examples change. Shared name-prefix tokens, dependency names, module deployment names, batch size, resource settings, parent module source/JSON/version, cleanup ownership and concurrency keys are unchanged by this follow-up. The changelog is preserved; BCPNFR22 does not require entries for test-only changes.

Restore bounded deployment retries for Azure's longer terminal-failure format: `failed with error(s). Showing 1 out of 1 error(s). Status Message: ... (Code: DeploymentFailed)`, including nested `ProvisioningDisabled` quota details. Classification still requires the current deployment name and the first error code in the failure summary. The older short format remains supported. Attempt limits, cleanup ownership, fixed parameters and existing transport, cancellation and unknown-outcome safeguards remain intact. Confirmed quota failures retry in the same region and subscription.

Recover typed HTTP request timeouts after submission by observing the original named deployment in its existing context, not by submitting a replacement. Use the appropriate read-only deployment cmdlet for resource-group, subscription, management-group and tenant scopes. Poll recognized in-progress states every 15 seconds for at most 60 minutes, stopping after three consecutive status-read timeouts. Confirmed success returns the normal outputs; only an observed Failed state enters the existing bounded deployment retry path. Recovered failures retain Azure's operation/provider error details and the original timeout. Failed diagnostic reads remain explicit failures with attempted names retained for cleanup. Authentication/transport errors, missing or ambiguous records, mismatched names, unknown states and exhausted recovery bounds do not permit resubmission. Genuine cancellation and PipelineStopped remain terminal. No workflow timeout settings, global HTTP configuration, SDK internals or cleanup authentication behavior are changed.

Move concurrency controls to the actual deployment and publication jobs, without changing trigger events, label gates or the dispatcher:

- Preselect subscriptions in the `avm-validation` environment using the existing variable/secret precedence, seeded shuffle, round-robin distribution and singleton fallback. Cross-job records carry the original pool index and SHA-256 digest of the canonical subscription GUID, never raw secret-backed identifiers or names. Variable-backed pools show their friendly names; secret-backed configurations show a generic subscription label.
- Before login, resolve exactly the preselected record and verify its ID digest. A changed record fails explicitly rather than selecting another subscription. Reuse that subscription through validation, deployment and cleanup.
- Every actual deployment holds the same module-plus-subscription inner lock through cleanup, independent of branch or shared-scope classification. Management-group, tenant and unresolved linked-template cases also take a distinct per-module outer lock, one test at a time. This preserves exclusion when different revisions add, remove or ignore a shared-scope test, without nested same-key deadlocks. Ordinary and ignored outer calls use unique run/attempt/module/test groups rather than the shared lock.
- Static and PSRule checks remain outside deployment locks. Publication and release-tag jobs retain a separate global per-module lock across legacy, preview, manual and publish-only entry points. All queues use `queue: max`; no active Azure work is automatically cancelled. Legacy entry workflows retain their existing outer scheduling.

Local verification for the naming follow-up: all four end-to-end scenarios compile with Bicep 0.47.16, and all 31 selected existing test-template static checks pass. Compiled-expression assertions confirm the full subscription/resource-group identity and identical instance names across init/idem, with serial batch size 1 unchanged. Native local Bicep evaluation confirms deterministic suffixes, changed suffixes for a different subscription or resource group, and valid 26-character names for every scenario using the configured `gci` prefix. Exact source comparison confirms the instance-name line is the only change in each test. The README was regenerated via dot-sourced `Set-AVMModule -SkipBuild -SkipFileAndFolderSetup`; the parent Bicep/JSON, version, changelog, utilities and workflows are unchanged by this follow-up.

The preceding timeout/concurrency follow-ups passed 690 targeted Pester cases: all 641 previous cases, including the original 191 retry/cleanup/regional regressions, plus 49 timeout-recovery cases. Coverage includes all four scopes, successful recovery with exactly one submission, bounded polling and status-read failures, cancellation, retained provider diagnostics, DoNotThrow, WhatIf, actual cleanup ownership, configuration precedence and secret-safe outputs, pre-login identity failures, cross-revision lock stability, every deployment caller, cleanup lock lifetime, fork isolation and unchanged trigger/manual-publication gates. All Azure interactions in these tests are mocked. Production helper analysis and whitespace checks passed.

The preceding SQL MI/concurrency changes also passed all 28 selected SQL MI static checks, including the original 17 description/ARM/changelog/version checks. The four real SQL MI matrix records were compiled and compared field-for-field against published commit `444e3c8`; the inner lock keys are exactly compatible and unchanged by subsequent follow-ups. Mixed-scope templates were also compiled locally. Actionlint passed with only its unsupported `queue` property diagnostic excluded; `queue: max` is documented GitHub syntax and separately asserted by the workflow tests. Existing Bicep API-age warnings remain in unchanged resources/dependencies.

## Summary

- Coordinate validation and deployment with at most **three distinct region candidates and three deployment attempts total**, rather than multiplying deployment retries by region.
- Allow an automatically selected test location to change after a deployment-stage regional failure only when the exact original deployment is authoritatively `Failed`, every structured error is regional, and its partial resources and deployment records are confirmed removed.
- Preserve existing safe same-region retries, timeout observation without resubmission, cancellation, pinned locations, global/resource-group-scoped tests, resource retention, fixed parameters and timestamps.
- Discover all deployment-operation pages, restore cross-subscription context, confirm supported soft-delete cleanup, remove child records before roots, and keep accurate outstanding cleanup names when cleanup only partly succeeds.
- Preserve original error records while redacting displayed parameter values, restore location-token files on failure, and reject invalid deployment-name prefixes instead of looping indefinitely.

This addresses the [deployment-stage VMSS capacity incident](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37110850292/job/111168628271), including the nested `InvalidTemplateDeployment` / `SkuNotAvailable` message without a top-level `DeploymentFailed` marker, and structured `ResourceDeploymentFailure` wrappers. `RequestDisallowedByAzure` with the documented `locationineligible` link remains eligible. Unknown/empty codes, unsupported-zone errors, mixed errors, authorization, quota and configuration errors do not authorize relocation.

## Scope

Independent infrastructure change based on `main`; **no `avm/` module files or READMEs changed**. Tests use synthetic templates and a synthetic provider/module identifier, not named AVM modules. Test-location changes remain in companion [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374). Subscription-feature registration is out of scope.

The existing `deploy_step` now performs validation and deployment together. Post-deployment checks and final-cleanup conditions remain unchanged. `removeDeployment=false` disables intermediate cleanup and deployment-stage relocation.

## Local verification

**515/515 tests passed** across:

- `Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1`
- `Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1`
- `RegionalValidationWorkflow.Tests.ps1`
- `DeploymentCleanupWorkflow.Tests.ps1`
- `CIParameterWorkflow.Tests.ps1`
- `TestSubscriptionWorkflow.Tests.ps1`

All 15 changed PowerShell files and nine action PowerShell blocks parse successfully (after substituting workflow expressions). The nine production PowerShell files have zero PSScriptAnalyzer warning/error findings. `git diff --check` passes.

**Mocked/offline verification only.** No Azure deployments, cloud mutations, workflow reruns, merges, or deployment-triggering labels were performed. Incomplete discovery, uncertain state, reserved soft-deleted resources, or unconfirmed removal stops relocation and preserves remaining cleanup tracking.

## Description

Adds optional Azure subscription feature registration before Bicep deployment tests. The deployment action reads a repository-root `.required-features.json` map from exact module paths to Terraform-compatible `"Namespace/FeatureName"` string arrays:

```json
{
  "avm/res/example/module": ["Microsoft.Example/FeatureOne"]
}
```

The entire map is validated before Azure calls. Missing files, missing exact keys and empty arrays are explicitly logged and skipped. Requirements are not inherited by parent or child modules. Duplicate keys/features, malformed arrays and invalid required values fail explicitly.

Registration runs after Azure login and before token replacement/validation, using the selected test subscription and the effective login tenant. It never switches accounts and verifies the Azure CLI context before making subscription-scoped calls. Static-only and ignored tests do not register features.

Behavior follows the existing Terraform implementation: skip `Registered`, register `NotRegistered`/`Unregistered`, wait without resubmitting `Registering`, then re-register and wait for the provider after each newly completed feature. Defaults are 60 checks with 10-second intervals and a 60-second command timeout. Approval requirements, unexpected states, authorization failures, malformed responses, cancellation and timeouts fail the gate. Registrations persist; nothing is unregistered.

Terraform source: [registration](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/blob/b0ba22f2fca81e4e068414e7f20bb703acd37de4/src/Avm.Authoring/Public/Register-AvmFeature.ps1), [manifest parsing](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/blob/b0ba22f2fca81e4e068414e7f20bb703acd37de4/src/Avm.Authoring/Private/Features/Read-AvmRequiredFeature.ps1), and [polling](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/blob/b0ba22f2fca81e4e068414e7f20bb703acd37de4/src/Avm.Authoring/Private/Features/Wait-AvmAzureRegistration.ps1).

This is an independent change from `main`. It deliberately does **not** create the root map or change any modules; the initial declaration belongs to [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374). Retry/cleanup code and shared environment setup are unchanged. No new dependencies are introduced. The test identity needs `Microsoft.Features/*` and the relevant provider `/register/action` permissions.

## Description

Narrow shared-tooling follow-up to https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7455, kept separate from the module/test changes in https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374.

The [observed deployment job](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37125785895/job/111211227311) stopped after its first attempt because `Get-ErrorMessageForScope -AsObject` tried to parse the Az operation cmdlet's `StatusMessage` as JSON. The [authoritative Az conversion](https://github.com/Azure/azure-powershell/blob/92febbd29ba5db3fc284e76549d8b014d508eadd/src/Resources/ResourceManager/SdkExtensions/NewResourcesExtensions.cs#L79-L95) actually assigns `result.Properties.StatusMessage?.Error?.ToFormattedString()` to that property. This change:

- Reads genuine ARM operation error objects only in the `-AsObject` path; keeps the existing non-structured Az display path intact.
- Extracts the existing scope/resource-ID and paginated operations reader into `sharedScripts\Get-DeploymentOperationAtScope.ps1` for reuse, avoiding circular script imports. Cleanup keeps its existing filtered behavior; structured inspection reads every operation type and every page.
- Rejects malformed/incomplete operation data, invalid or out-of-scope continuation links, failed page retrieval, and nonterminal states. Retrieval failures produce sanitized diagnostics without raw response contents; cancellation still propagates.
- Replaces JSON-string cmdlet mocks with SDK-formatted text and genuine raw operation responses, using generic shared-tooling fixtures. Covers successful relocation, all four scopes, pagination, mixed/unknown/blank-code/missing errors, cleanup ordering, retained deployment names, redaction, and existing retry budgets.

### Verified built-in applications

| `DevOpsInfrastructure` | `31687f79-5e43-4c1e-8c63-d9f4bff5cf8b` | `devOpsInfrastructureObjectID` |

**Deployment prerequisite:** provider registration and the corresponding tenant service principals must already exist. Read-only queries by application ID found all three absent from the current CI tenant. This change deliberately does not create them or register providers. The CI identity's Directory Readers access is an agreed prerequisite. No directory roles, app permissions, service principals, or secrets were added.

- `CI_DEV_OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE_OBJECT_ID`

## Pipeline Reference

<!-- Insert your Pipeline Status Badge below -->

| Pipeline |
| -------- |
| Azure deployment and deployment validation: **not run**, as explicitly requested. No workflow reruns or deployment-enabling labels were applied. |

### Local validation

The following results record the initial direct-Graph change. See **Final static-compatibility validation** below for the current, complete validation results.

Bicep CLI: `0.47.16`. Commands below ran locally before the commit; `$out` and `$log` refer to session-only compiler artifact paths. `$file` covered every changed entrypoint listed above.

| Exact command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `bicep build $file.FullName --outfile (Join-Path $out "$stem.json")` | Passed for all 20 original entrypoints, before editing. |

| `Set-AVMModule -ModuleFolderPath $modulePath -SkipFileAndFolderSetup -SkipBuild -SkipVersionCheck -ForceCacheRefresh` | Completed for all nine exact module folders, after dot-sourcing `utilities\tools\Set-AVMModule.ps1`, with isolated process `TEMP`/`TMP`. Generated README contents were unchanged, so no documentation changes are included. |
| `Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration` | Passed: **456 passed, 0 failed, 77 existing suite skips**; 383 unrelated tests not selected. Configuration below. |
| `git diff --cached --check` | Passed. |

Pester used the existing repository compliance suite, with only the relevant module and test-template checks selected. The README parity test was explicitly excluded to prevent it from resetting generated files.

```powershell
$modulePaths = @(
  'avm\res\dev-ops-infrastructure\pool'
  'avm\res\azure-stack-hci\cluster'
  'avm\res\azure-stack-hci\virtual-machine-instance'

)

$configuration = New-PesterConfiguration
$configuration.Run.Container = New-PesterContainer -Path '.\utilities\pipelines\staticValidation\compliance\module.tests.ps1' -Data @{
  repoRootPath = (Get-Location).Path
  moduleFolderPaths = @($modulePaths | ForEach-Object { (Resolve-Path $_).Path })
}
$configuration.Run.PassThru = $true
$configuration.Filter.Tag = @('Template', 'TestTemplate')
$configuration.Filter.ExcludeTag = @('Readme')
```

Additional in-process checks passed for all 20 compiled templates: exactly one Graph node per entrypoint, `existing: true`, the verified application ID, the correct `.id` handoff, no removed top-level CI parameter, identical remaining parameter definitions, and identical nested deployment templates. Whole-file comparisons against the original source confirmed that only the intended extension, parameter removal, lookup, and ID handoff changed. A repository-wide `main.test.bicep` scan found no remaining declarations for these three external built-in object-ID inputs.

The existing suite reports warnings about unchanged public-module object types; these are not new failures. No public module, version, changelog, or coverage exclusions were changed.

### Final static-compatibility validation

The initial targeted checks above did not exercise PSRule's offline expansion. Commit [`96cbadd1b`](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/commit/96cbadd1bce9c5a50a55cc0a64e2b2771cd2d8f1) repairs that regression in all 20 entrypoints. Each fixture accepts nullable `builtInServicePrincipalObjectId` **without a Bicep default**. When it is omitted, the conditional `existing` resource resolves the same verified application through Graph; when supplied, the unchanged dependency/public parameter receives the override instead.

The shared `utilities\pipelines\staticValidation\psrule\ps-rule.yaml` supplies `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` through `AZURE_PARAMETER_DEFAULTS` **only during static analysis**. All 2,891 complete rule records match, including target name/type, rule, outcome, and reason; per-run coverage and warnings also match. |

For the final PSRule run, `$psruleOptions` was exactly `.\utilities\pipelines\staticValidation\psrule\ps-rule.yaml`, using the committed on-disk configuration rather than an in-memory override. The existing module-workflow matrix selected all **18 defaults/WAF scenarios**, including unchanged DevOps Pools defaults, and all four required/optional CI baselines. Local references and tokens were handled with the existing `Get-LocallyReferencedFileList` and `Convert-TokensInFileList` helpers, using identical non-sensitive values on both sides and `namePrefix = 'gci'`. ## Description

Releases the `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/virtual-machine-instance` changes from #7429, which were merged but never published, as `0.3.0`. MCR's latest version is still `0.1.2`.

### Why `0.2.0` was never published

- After #7429 merged, the module pipeline on `main` failed the static test "Set-ModuleReadMe script should not apply any updates": the README's cross-reference to `avm/res/hybrid-compute/machine` was out of date.
- #7430 fixed the README. README-only changes don't trigger the module pipeline, and a manual run on `main` then passed all checks but skipped tag creation, because a release is only created when the last commit changes `main.json` or `version.json`.

### This PR

- `version.json`: `0.2` → `0.3`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: renames the unpublished `## 0.2.0` section to `## 0.3.0`, with the same changes and a note that `0.2.0` was never published.

There are no template changes: `main.bicep`, `main.json` and the README are unchanged, and running `Set-AVMModule` with fresh caches produces no changes.

### Changes released with `0.3.0` (from #7429)

| Resource type or reference | Published `0.1.2` | `0.3.0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines` (`existing` reference) | `2023-10-03-preview` | `2026-07-15` |
| `avm/res/hybrid-compute/machine` (referenced module) | `0.4.1` (creates the Arc machine with `2024-07-10`) | `0.6.0` (creates it with `2026-07-15`) |
| `Microsoft.Resources/deployments` (AVM telemetry) | `2024-03-01` | `2025-04-01` |

`Microsoft.AzureStackHCI/virtualMachineInstances` stays on `2024-01-01`. No parameters or outputs change.

### Versioning

The pipeline resets the patch version when `version.json` changes, so this merge publishes `0.3.0`; the pipeline's `Get-ModuleTargetVersion` returns `0.3.0` for this branch. `0.2.0` won't exist: consumers move from `0.1.2` to `0.3.0`, which contains exactly the changes listed for `0.2.0`.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule` with fresh caches: no changes.
- The module workflow ran on this branch with static validation ([run 37268612363](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37268612363)): 92 static tests passed, including all `CHANGELOG.md` tests ("must contain a section for the module version", "must contain only versions, that are published"), and all PSRule checks passed.
- This module's deployment tests are skipped by its `.e2eignore` files, like the other Azure Stack HCI modules, so the publish step runs after the merge.
- The template is unchanged since #7429, which was validated end-to-end on Azure Local: a VM instance deployment, and a re-deployment with the final change (`machine` `0.6.0`) that left the VM and its Arc machine unchanged.

Repair shared cleanup and retry failures observed in [run 37438688587](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37438688587), retaining the original narrowly qualified missing-child preflight fix.

This is the consolidated tooling review: it includes the Cosmos classifier from [#7465](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7465), the AKS classifier from [#7467](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7467), and the complete twelve-file non-`avm/` slice from [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374), including its held Image Builder repair. All twelve transferred blobs exactly match source commit `3eb4712cdcc89d6b50a8069f080bb1cca9d09f00`; there were no source-content deviations. The module source branch was not merged into this history. There are no `avm/` differences from main `956e47dc71e85e0c8307edd4fc70418b14c840c8`.

- **Missing preflight child:** only a failed parent's unique failed Create with matching direct preflight evidence and an exact child-record `404 DeploymentNotFound` permits omission. Successful siblings and owned resources still require cleanup.
- **Existing Graph lookup:** an ID-less successful Create is omitted from resource deletion only when that exact deployment's server-exported template proves a literal `existing: true` service-principal declaration. Symbol, type, import alias, provider and version must match uniquely. Missing export access, malformed/duplicate metadata and unproven declarations block strict cleanup; parent proof is never reused for a child.
- **Asynchronous history deletion:** after an accepted DELETE, confirm absence with at most three exact-record GETs, 15 seconds apart only while a terminal record remains visible. Preserve pending root ownership for final cleanup instead of rediscovering an already-deleted root for 39 minutes. Do not repeat DELETE or claim removal before confirmation.
- **ACI capacity:** recognize only the captured documented, message-only capacity leaf for a current-subscription container group in the selected location, with a standard-size Linux request. Generic messages, explicit unknown/empty codes, quota and mixed failures remain ineligible.
- **ML workspace Cosmos capacity:** retain the exact structured workspace failure and embedded Cosmos high-demand response, requiring the named region to match the selected location. Generic `BadRequest`, region-access/quota guesses, malformed payloads and mixed errors do not qualify.
- **AKS empty-zone preflight:** retain the exact managed-cluster preflight response where supported zones are explicitly empty in the selected region. General unsupported-zone messages, a different region, ambiguous metadata and mixed errors remain ineligible.
- **Intentional same-region exception:** add a new, narrowly supported transient-deployment path, rather than classifying generic HTTP 500 as regional. Every error leaf must be `InternalServerError` under a matching resource failure for `Microsoft.Network/applicationGateways`, `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers` or `Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints`. Require the exact Failed root, complete terminal discovery, **no deployment scripts anywhere in the discovered attempt**, and verified resource/history removal before replay. Validation-stage 500, mixed/unknown/auth failures, unsupported targets, pins, global or resource-group scope, retained resources and ambiguous/nonterminal roots do not enable this path.

Original errors, remaining deployment names, context restoration and the three-region/three-submission limits are preserved. Mixed regional/transient attempts revalidate only when changing regions. No `avm/` fixtures, public module APIs, package dependencies or broad unsupported-region/zone/quota rules are changed.

### Transferred tooling

- Image Builder startup waits for the newly submitted run, not an earlier success or the completion of the run request. Waiting is bounded by the build timeout plus five minutes; explicit asynchronous mode remains supported. VHD copying requires a successful build, waits up to five minutes for one valid output, resolves one source/destination storage context, and checks a requested completed copy.
- The replication-region helper selects a provider-supported secondary region, preferring the paired region before deterministic recommendation/geography fallbacks. The FinOps Hub workflow exposes its existing location override as an optional dispatch input.
- `.required-features.json` declares the VMSS `Microsoft.Compute/EncryptionAtHost` prerequisite for the existing deployment-only registration path. No feature was registered during this work.
- Agent setup registers the default PowerShell Gallery only when absent, respecting `ShouldProcess` and surfacing discovery/registration failures.
- README generation preserves quoted values and URLs when stripping inline comments, prefers canonical resource metadata, and retains explicit failure for malformed metadata.
- Static PSRule analysis preserves the shared `builtInServicePrincipalObjectId` placeholder `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`. The HCI prerequisite helper uses Key Vault API `2026-02-01` for its vault and five secrets without changing its RBAC setting.

**Remaining limitation:** the captured Application Gateway WAF and managed-environment max failures include deployment scripts, so they remain ineligible for the new same-region replay path. Resource/history absence does not prove delayed script deletion work has finished. Their provider failures still need a future authorized run; this change does not claim they are repaired. Graph omission also remains conditional on successful exact-template export. No live Azure validation was performed.

### Validation

Offline reproductions failed before the corresponding shared repairs: 17 history-removal cases, 17 Graph-proof cases, four transient-eligibility controls, and five script-replay/root-state controls. The consolidated run passed **1,521 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 not run**. This includes all **1,353 tests in the nine requested suites**:

| Suite | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| `Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1` | 479 |
| `DeploymentCleanupWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 149 |
| `Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1` | 365 |
| `RegionalValidationWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 21 |
| `CIParameterWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 11 |
| `ModuleWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 253 |
| `ImageBuilderScripts.Tests.ps1` | 53 |
| `ModuleReadMeStaticValidation.Tests.ps1` | 16 |
| `Set-EnvironmentOnAgent.Tests.ps1` | 6 |

Additional relevant coverage passed **168 tests**:

| Suite | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| `Set-ModuleReadme.Tests.ps1` | 4 |
| `ModuleReadMeNotices.Tests.ps1` | 5 |
| `Register-RequiredSubscriptionFeature.Tests.ps1` | 134 |
| `RequiredSubscriptionFeaturesWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 8 |
| Private `ConsolidatedToolingHelpers.Tests.ps1` | 17 |

The private supplemental fixture checks paired/fallback region selection, rejection and error propagation, FinOps input forwarding, the exact feature map and static GUID. It is retained with the validation reports, not added to the transferred source slice. Azure calls and repository registration are mocked; process TEMP/TMP is isolated.

Executed test inputs and commands follow. `$artifacts` is the private validation artifact directory containing the supplemental fixture; only its machine-specific value is omitted.

```powershell
$repoRoot = (Get-Location).Path
Import-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.0.0 -ErrorAction Stop
Import-Module powershell-yaml -ErrorAction Stop

    'Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1'

$additional = @(
    'Set-ModuleReadme.Tests.ps1'

)

```

Result: **passed, 1,521/1,521**. All added tests from both classifier inputs survive. The Graph predicate also matched the three supplied full CI-compiled fixture templates (Linux max, Windows max and WAF).


Result: **passed, 64/64**, including all **18 generic InternalServerError regional-negative controls**. `$replayHarness` is the coordinator's private captured-error harness. The adapter loads the actual shared classifier helper and obtains subscription context only from each exact captured root deployment ID; it changes none of the 64 assertions or expectations.

```powershell
Import-Module PSScriptAnalyzer -ErrorAction Stop
$paths = @(
    '.\utilities\pipelines\e2eValidation\resourceDeployment\Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.ps1'
    '.\utilities\pipelines\e2eValidation\resourceRemoval\Initialize-DeploymentRemoval.ps1'

$findings = @($paths | ForEach-Object {
```

Results: **10 production scripts checked; 0 integration-only findings**. The complete scope has seven inherited warnings: six already present before transfer in agent setup/README generation, plus the source helper's `DeploymentScriptOutputs` assignment consumed by the Azure deployment-script host. The README helper also emits one pre-existing unmatched `ResourceTypesToExclude` suppression diagnostic; it occurs in both the destination baseline and frozen source.
